title: Inverse image of Tate twists
statement:
Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible, and let
$\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\cO_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Qlb\}$ be admissible. There are canonical
isomorphisms
$$
f^{-1}\mu_{\ell^n,Y}\cong\mu_{\ell^n,X},\qquad
f^{-1}\bigl(\Lambda_Y(d)\bigr)\cong\Lambda_X(d)\quad(d\in\mathbf Z),
$$
compatible with the isomorphism $\alpha_f\colon f^{-1}\Lambda_Y\cong\Lambda_X$ of
[lem-sfb-alpha-iso] and the module structures, and with the Kummer transition maps.
Consequently $f^*(K(d))\cong(f^*K)(d)$ for $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$.

proof.text: Use the local-ring residue criterion and the sheaf criterion for units to show that ell, and hence ell^n, is a global unit on X and Y. Apply finiteRootSiteComparison with the finite auxiliary ring ULift(ZMod(ell^n)); its normalized root square expresses the prescribed pro-etale root comparison as a composite of isomorphisms. This includes n=0 and the zero auxiliary ring.

Construct the coefficient ring comparison from the normalized abelian comparison. Pullback-forget comparison and its unit equation show sectionwise that addition, multiplication, zero and one are preserved. The abelian comparison is an isomorphism, so this lifts to the commutative-ring sheaf isomorphism. Its adjunct is precisely the prescribed condensed coefficient map; adjunction and faithfulness prove uniqueness.

Lift the root direct-image map to the constant Z/ell^(r+1)-module structure; additive homomorphisms preserve this scalar action. Its adjoint is invertible because the underlying abelian map is the root comparison composed with the normalized pullback-forget unit mate. Extension of finite scalars commutes with pullback by the tensor universal property. On pure tensors this gives exactly the coefficient/root formula. Adjunction, pure-tensor generation, and the root transition square prove compatibility with every Kummer identification.

Use preservation of the native integral Tate tower cone, isolated in lem-pur-native-integral-tate-tower-limit. Each finite abelian component comparison is invertible; postcomposition by this natural isomorphism gives a limiting cone, and the previously projection-normalized integral comparison is its unique limiting-cone map, hence invertible. Lift it using the integral residue tensor square. Scalar extension then constructs the rational comparison; its adjunction proves localization normalization and uniqueness. The unique coefficient and projection formulas prove naturality under every finite field inclusion. Colimit preservation yields the algebraic-closure comparison. For its coefficient action, use the existing proved isColimitPadicAlgClRingObjCocone: it is the image of the point finite-subextension cocone under upperStarFromPoint. To prove its semilinearity, test on tensor products of coefficient and module coprojections, choose a common finite upper field, and use the normalized finite-stage actions and naturality there.

source.place: Integral twist; Rational and algebraic closure paragraphs

proof.text: The common root cover supplies rank-one trivializations for all finite, integral, rational and algebraic-closure lines. Identify the actual section-module pullback with the generic ringed-site pullback by uniqueness of left adjoints, retaining its unit formula. For internal modules, the normalized direct-image coefficient map and equivalence-square adjunction comparison give the corresponding linear lift with its exact abelian adjunct. Apply the signed-line derived base-change theorem to each degree-one isomorphism. Its unit, tensor and evaluation formulas yield the required zero, positive and negative normalizations; derived natural-isomorphism transport gives the consequence for every unbounded complex. Both tensor-power presentations are the same canonical recursive construction after the recorded abbreviation repair.
